title: Clawback Reserve on Re-Sent Payouts — Cartwise Shopper Payouts Training Notes
content:
Training notes for the Shopper Payments desk: the clawback reserve kept back from a re-sent returned payout on Cartwise Shopper Payouts.

> A clawback reserve is kept back from the re-send: a shopper with two or more batch pay reversals in the last 12 months keeps back 20.00, a shopper with exactly one keeps back 10.00, and a shopper with none keeps back nothing.

**What counts as a batch pay reversal?**
A pay reversal booked on one of the shopper's batches in Cartwise Shopper Batches. Tip reductions are not pay reversals and are not counted here.

**What does "the last 12 months" mean?**
The reversals booked fewer than 12 whole months before the day of the re-send. A reversal booked exactly 12 whole months before that day, or earlier, is not counted.

**What happens to the reserve?**
The reserve is taken off the amount drawn for the re-send and stays on the unpaid earnings balance; the re-send never falls below zero.

**Reserve by count.**

| Batch pay reversals in the last 12 months | Kept back |
|---|---|
| 0 | Nothing |
| 1 | 10.00 |
| 2 | 20.00 |
| 3 or more | 20.00 |

**Hypothetical pair.** A shopper whose batches show one pay reversal booked 11 months before the re-send and another booked 13 months before has exactly one in the last 12 months, so 10.00 is kept back. Had the second reversal been booked 9 months before, the count would be two and 20.00 would be kept back.
